tagline: Chart the whole suite in one place.
intro: Bench is the read-and-visualize layer over the rest of BigBlueBam. You assemble dashboards out of widgets, where each widget queries an approved data source like Bond deals or Blast campaigns and renders a chart, KPI card, or table. Bench never stores your business data; it reads other products' tables through an allowlisted registry and scopes every query to your active organization. By the end of this chapter you will be able to build a dashboard, explore a source ad hoc, save and schedule queries, and see where an agent can summarize a dashboard and flag anomalies for you.
atAGlance: Shared dashboards built from widgets, each charting one registered data source
Eleven chart types, from bar and line to KPI card, gauge, and progress bar
Ad-Hoc Explorer for a quick aggregate without building a whole dashboard
Saved queries and cron-driven scheduled reports to Email, Banter, or Brief
Full MCP surface, so an agent can read dashboards, run queries, and compare periods

pullQuotes.after: always scopes every query to your active organization
pullQuotes.text: Bench reads other apps but never writes them, and every query is org-scoped through an allowlisted registry.

pullQuotes.after: compares the most recent period against the previous one
pullQuotes.text: An agent can flag a metric that moved sharply, marking any change over thirty percent as high, medium, or low severity.

callouts.after: pick one of the eleven types
callouts.text: The Widget Wizard and the Widget Edit page offer the same eleven chart types, but Widget Edit adds a live preview that re-runs the query as you change the source, measures, and dimensions. Tune there when you want to see the result before you save.

callouts.after: Three are exposed to you as queryable
callouts.text: A materialized view is a pre-computed rollup the worker refreshes for you. Bench surfaces three as bench: data sources: Daily Task Throughput, Pipeline Snapshot, and Campaign Engagement.

callouts.after: report delivery is a stub in this release
callouts.text: Send now and the schedule only stamp the row's status; they do not produce or send an actual PDF, email, Banter post, or Brief document. A successful run even shows the neutral gray pill rather than a green one, so treat this as wiring, not confirmed delivery.

callouts.after: the first measure with its first aggregation
callouts.text: Open the Explorer, pick Knowledge Base Articles from the Data Source dropdown, and click Run Query to see the fixed shape: the first measure, the first two dimensions, and up to fifty rows.

quiz.q: What does Bench store about your business data?
choices: A full copy of every source table
Only the dashboards and widgets you build
Nothing; it queries other products' tables through a registry
A nightly snapshot of all org data
quiz.answer: Nothing; it queries other products' tables through a registry

quiz.q: How many chart types does the Widget Wizard offer at the Chart Type step?
What are the three visibility options a dashboard can have?
What is the minimum number of measures a query needs?
Name the five numeric aggregations a measure can use.
quiz.answer: count, sum, avg, min, or max.

quiz.q: When you duplicate a dashboard, what visibility does the copy get?
What query shape runs when you pick a source manually in the Explorer?
choices: Every measure and dimension for the source
The first measure with its first aggregation, plus the first two dimensions, limited to 50 rows
A custom query you type in
quiz.answer: The first measure with its first aggregation, plus the first two dimensions, limited to 50 rows

quiz.q: What are the three delivery methods for a scheduled report?
quiz.answer: Email, Banter Channel, and Brief Document.

quiz.q: What are the three export formats for a scheduled report?
Why do the helpdesk:tickets and Daily Task Throughput sources return no data in this release?
quiz.answer: Their backing tables have no organization column, so the query builder's org filter fails and the query returns nothing.
quiz.where: Sources that do not return data

quiz.q: At what change does bench_detect_anomalies flag a metric, and with what severities?
choices: Over 30%, with high, medium, or low severity
Over 50%, with a single alert flag
Any change, ranked one through five
quiz.answer: Over 30%, with high, medium, or low severity

quiz.q: What are the read-only values shown in Bench Settings for Cache TTL and the statement timeout?
quiz.answer: The Default Cache TTL is 60 seconds and the Statement Timeout is 10,000 ms.
